bibl.title: Effects of concurrent caffeine and mobile phone exposure on local target probability processing in the human brain

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether caffeine and UMTS mobile-phone irradiation interact to affect target probability processing
span.quote: Millions of people use mobile phones (MP) while drinking coffee or other caffeine containing beverages. Little is known about the potential combined effects of MP irradiation and caffeine on cognitive functions.

span.label: whether combined caffeine and mobile phone exposure affects reaction time and pre-target brain oscillations more than either alone
span.quote: Our hypothesis was that, due to previously reported 1 , 6 similar facilitatory effects on brain excitatory activity, simultaneous caffeine and MP exposure will have a larger effect than caffeine or MP EMF exposure alone.

span.label: a full-factorial, pharmacologically validated null on mobile-phone exposure, alongside positive caffeine effects on reaction time and alpha amplitude
span.quote: However, in the present pharmacologically validated study UMTS exposure either alone or in combination with caffeine did not alter RT or pre-stimulus oscillatory brain activity.

span.label: null-result
span.quote: However, in the present pharmacologically validated study UMTS exposure either alone or in combination with caffeine did not alter RT or pre-stimulus oscillatory brain activity.

span.label: caffeine and mobile-phone RF exposure effects on visual target detection
span.quote: Here we investigated whether caffeine intake and concurrent exposure to Universal Mobile Telecommunications System (UMTS) MP-like irradiation may interactively influence neuro-cognitive function in an active visual oddball paradigm.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: In a full factorial experimental design, 25 participants performed a simple visual target detection task while reaction time (RT) and electroencephalogram (EEG) was recorded.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Caffeine raises the arousal state, which suppresses pre-target alpha oscillations and thereby improves visual perceptual performance
span.quote: One possible explanation of the decreased alpha band activity in the pre-target by caffeine may be that caffeine increased the arousal state, thus promoted better visual perception performance compared to the control condition 54 .

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Caffeine increases sensitivity to the regularity of the stimulus sequence, making implicit short-term memory for the preceding standards more efficient and so speeding responses to expected targets
span.quote: Thus, it would be reasonable to conclude that caffeine increases the sensitivity to the stimulus pattern, and improves the efficiency of implicit short-term memory 41 .

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Alternative account: caffeine acts only at the motor end, speeding the initiation of an already prepared response rather than altering expectancy-related cognition
span.quote: Namely, caffeine only facilitates the faster initiation of an already prepared response, independently of the underlying differential cognitive processes (e.g., higher or lower stimulus expectancy).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A drop in gamma-band activity before an anticipated target frees processing for the incoming task-relevant stimulus, speeding its detection
span.quote: Thus, it is likely that the decreased gamma activity prior to the predicted arrival of a target stimulus may facilitate the processing of relevant task-related information 36 .

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Caffeine and mobile-phone EMF were expected to combine because both act on calcium-dependent signalling, which underlies cognitive function
span.quote: While calcium plays an important role in cognitive functions 20 , 21 , 22 , any combined effects of caffeine and MP exposure on calcium related mechanisms may affect cognitive performance indexed by reaction time and brain oscillatory activity.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Proposed reason for the UMTS null result: the modulation used was biologically ineffective or the field intensity fell below the threshold for any detectable biological effect
span.quote: A possible explanation for lack of UMTS exposure effects may be that the applied signal modulation was ineffective or the signal intensity was too low, i.e., under the threshold for detectable biological effects.

span.label: caffeine is used as a pharmacological positive control, on the grounds that this dose reliably improves cognition
span.quote: Caffeine exposure also served as pharmacological (positive) control as it has been previously reported that intraoral administration of 3 mg/kg b.w. caffeine reliably improved cognitive functions and mood

span.label: saliva caffeine concentration is measured by HPLC at the start and end of each session, so the exposure is verified rather than assumed
span.quote: Saliva samples were taken at the beginning and the end of each recording session and caffeine concentrations were determined by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC).

span.label: an additive model tests synergy directly: the sum of the two single-agent differences is compared against the combined condition
span.quote: To reveal potential interactions of caffeine and UMTS MP exposure in RT and oscillatory measures we focused on the exposure block and we used the additive analysis model with the following formula, as applied elsewhere 42 , 43 , 44 : Hereafter, “[Caffeine − Control] + [UMTS − Control]” and “Combined − Control” are referred to as ‘sum’ and ‘simultaneous’ data, respectively. We hypothesized that violation of the additivity of the analyzed RT or spectral amplitude measures would indicate synergistic interactions.

span.label: dose is individualised at 3 mg/kg body weight, averaging 211.56 mg
span.quote: Three mg/kg caffeine packed in identical hard gelatin capsules were administered to the participants. The capsules were administered per os with 200 ml still mineral water. We used 5, 10, 20, and 100 mg caffeine-filled capsules. The average body weight was 70.52 kg (SEM: 3.66) and the average caffeine dose was 211.56 mg (SEM: 10.98).

span.label: identical capsule counts in placebo and caffeine sessions, to stop participants inferring their condition from the number swallowed
span.quote: To avoid possible influences caused by subjective bias on the number of capsules taken, volunteers received the same amount of capsules in the control (placebo) sessions as in the caffeine sessions.

span.label: only non-smokers enrolled, because smoking cuts caffeine half-life by 30 to 50%
span.quote: Because the half-life of caffeine in the body is reduced by 30 to 50% in smokers compared to nonsmokers 13 , here we enrolled only nonsmokers.

span.label: The null UMTS result may reflect an ineffective modulation or a signal intensity below the threshold for biological effects rather than a true absence of any mobile-phone effect.
span.quote: A possible explanation for lack of UMTS exposure effects may be that the applied signal modulation was ineffective or the signal intensity was too low, i.e., under the threshold for detectable biological effects.

span.label: The task design cannot decide between the two competing explanations of the caffeine benefit (increased sensitivity to the stimulus pattern versus faster initiation of an already prepared response).
span.quote: However, to draw the final conclusion we suggest that future studies with more focused task design should address this question.

span.label: the treatment main effect on overall reaction time did not survive post hoc testing
span.quote: However the Treatment effect did not survive the post hoc analyses.

span.label: the paper's own preferred interpretation is undercut by its regression models, which show no probability-by-treatment interaction
span.quote: However, the results of the multiple regression models showed no interaction effects between the target Probability and Treatments which support a different possible explanation of the present results. Namely, caffeine only facilitates the faster initiation of an already prepared response, independently of the underlying differential cognitive processes (e.g., higher or lower stimulus expectancy).

span.label: the authors call for a more focused task design before concluding
span.quote: However, to draw the final conclusion we suggest that future studies with more focused task design should address this question.

span.label: attrition: two participants dropped from the reaction time analysis and four from the EEG analysis
span.quote: Due to excessive artifacts or data loss, four participants were excluded from further analysis. The final sample in the spectral amplitude analysis comprised data of 21 participants (11 female, mean age 20.48 years, SD 1.4).

span.label: the same dataset was already analysed in a previous paper for evoked potentials
span.quote: Here we analyzed the recorded data in conjunction with a previous study 5 in a different aspect. In a previous paper we analyzed the potential effects of caffeine and EMF on stimulus-evoked brain potentials (P300). Here we focus on spectral power of pre-target oscillatory activity because several studies found that caffeine and EMF alters brain oscillations.

span.label: the hypothesis stated at the outset - that combined exposure would exceed either alone - was not supported
span.quote: In addition, the present results do not support the notion that UMTS exposure may strengthen the observed facilitatory effects of caffeine on RT in a combined or synergistic manner

span.label: the additive-model test for drug synergy, applied to a drug and a physical exposure
span.quote: To reveal potential interactions of caffeine and UMTS MP exposure in RT and oscillatory measures we focused on the exposure block and we used the additive analysis model with the following formula, as applied elsewhere 42 , 43 , 44 : Hereafter, “[Caffeine − Control] + [UMTS − Control]” and “Combined − Control” are referred to as ‘sum’ and ‘simultaneous’ data, respectively. We hypothesized that violation of the additivity of the analyzed RT or spectral amplitude measures would indicate synergistic interactions.

span.label: HPLC assay of saliva, used to verify that the pharmacological manipulation actually took effect
span.quote: Saliva samples were taken at the beginning and the end of each recording session and caffeine concentrations were determined by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC).

span.label: matching the NUMBER of capsules between placebo and caffeine sessions, not merely their contents
span.quote: To avoid possible influences caused by subjective bias on the number of capsules taken, volunteers received the same amount of capsules in the control (placebo) sessions as in the caffeine sessions.

span.label: a two-position switch on the RF amplifier setting genuine or sham exposure, so neither party could tell which was running - the threat is named only by the word blind, which is why this is scored lower
span.quote: Double-blind experimental conditions were ensured by a two-position switch (A or B) located on the front panel of the RF amplifier: one position was associated with genuine exposure, and the other with sham exposure.

span.label: Low and High probability are stipulated as exactly one versus exactly four preceding standards, on the ground that prior work found no further change beyond four
span.quote: We used the terms of Low and High because prior studies have shown no difference between the RTs to targets if the number of the preceding standard stimuli were more than four 41 . Thus Low (Prob1) and High (Prob4) can be considered as most representative categories to describe the possible involvement of different target expectancy levels in task performance.

span.label: pharmacologically validated means the study contains an agent known to produce an effect, so a null on the other agent is a null in a demonstrably sensitive assay
span.quote: Caffeine exposure also served as pharmacological (positive) control as it has been previously reported that intraoral administration of 3 mg/kg b.w. caffeine reliably improved cognitive functions and mood

span.label: synergy is operationalised as a violation of additivity - the sum of single-agent effects against the combined condition, not as a simple interaction term
span.quote: To reveal potential interactions of caffeine and UMTS MP exposure in RT and oscillatory measures we focused on the exposure block and we used the additive analysis model with the following formula, as applied elsewhere 42 , 43 , 44 : Hereafter, “[Caffeine − Control] + [UMTS − Control]” and “Combined − Control” are referred to as ‘sum’ and ‘simultaneous’ data, respectively. We hypothesized that violation of the additivity of the analyzed RT or spectral amplitude measures would indicate synergistic interactions.

span.label: replicates → Foxe et al. (reference 24), who found with a go/no-go task that caffeine decreased pre-target alpha power
span.quote: In the present study we used a simple visual oddball paradigm and we also found that caffeine decreased the pre-target alpha power both in Low and High target probability conditions.

span.label: replicates → Gomez and co-workers (reference 36), who reported reduced pre-target gamma power speeding up processing of the forthcoming target
span.quote: In line with their results, in the present study, in the pre-target period, we found lower gamma amplitude with faster RT in the High local probability condition and higher gamma amplitude with slower RT in the Low local probability condition.

span.label: extends → Trunk et al. (reference 5), the authors' own earlier P300/ERP analysis of the same dataset
span.quote: These null effects of UMTS exposure on visual discrimination are in line our previous report on the same behavioral dataset 5 where we found that the UMTS exposure had no observable modulatory effects on RT and P300 ERP measures either alone or in combination with caffeine.

span.label: confirms → previous studies finding no effect of UMTS exposure on reaction time
span.quote: In line with the results of previous studies 50 , 51 we found no evidence that UMTS exposure alters RT.

span.label: supports → the established finding that caffeine decreases reaction time and reduces alpha power
span.quote: Tukey HSD post hoc analysis revealed significant amplitude decrease of both alpha bands [alpha1 (p < 0.005), alpha2 (p < 0.005)] in the caffeine treatment compared to control.

span.label: contradicts → the authors' own prior hypothesis of a synergistic caffeine-by-EMF effect
span.quote: Our hypothesis was that, due to previously reported 1 , 6 similar facilitatory effects on brain excitatory activity, simultaneous caffeine and MP exposure will have a larger effect than caffeine or MP EMF exposure alone.

span.label: qualifies → its own implicit short-term memory interpretation, on the basis of the regression results
span.quote: However, the results of the multiple regression models showed no interaction effects between the target Probability and Treatments which support a different possible explanation of the present results. Namely, caffeine only facilitates the faster initiation of an already prepared response, independently of the underlying differential cognitive processes (e.g., higher or lower stimulus expectancy).

span.label: caffeine —causes→ reaction time
span.quote: The Tukey HSD post hoc test indicated that the High RT shortened in the caffeine (p < 0.039) and combined (p < 0.023) treatments compared to control

span.label: caffeine —causes→ alpha
span.quote: Tukey HSD post hoc analysis revealed significant amplitude decrease of both alpha bands [alpha1 (p < 0.005), alpha2 (p < 0.005)] in the caffeine treatment compared to control.

span.label: alpha —operationalised-as→ arousal
span.quote: Caffeine also decreased pre-target alpha amplitude resulting in higher arousal level.

span.label: local probability —causes→ reaction time
span.quote: The analysis of the Low (mean: 442.22 ms, SEM: 10.16) and High (mean: 398.54 ms, SEM: 9.71) probability categories revealed that they significantly differed from each other [F(1,22) = 102.584, p < 0.001, eta-squared = 0.823].

span.label: UMTS —distinct-from→ caffeine
span.quote: However, in the present pharmacologically validated study UMTS exposure either alone or in combination with caffeine did not alter RT or pre-stimulus oscillatory brain activity.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: As data followed a normal distribution (determined by Shapiro-Wilk tests), repeated measures analysis of variance (rANOVA) was used to compare the means between groups.

span.label: Shapiro-Wilk normality test
span.quote: As data followed a normal distribution (determined by Shapiro-Wilk tests), repeated measures analysis of variance (rANOVA) was used to compare the means between groups.

span.label: Tukey HSD post hoc test
span.quote: Where main effects or interactions were found, statistical results were further specified by post hoc Tukey’s honestly significant difference (HSD).

span.label: effect size
span.quote: Each P-value with partial eta- squared estimates of effect size are given in the Results Section.

span.label: p-value
span.quote: The null hypothesis was rejected at a significance level of 0.05 (alpha).

span.label: t-test
span.quote: We also analyzed possible probability effects with Student’s t-test in each Treatment condition separately.

span.label: correlation
span.quote: Kendall’s correlation also showed that RT marginally decreased

span.label: regression
span.quote: Multiple regression statistical method was used to address the question how the different treatments contributed to behavioral effects observed in RT measures controlling for probability categories, and pre-target EEG amplitudes.

span.label: mean
span.quote: Twenty-five healthy, right-handed, non-smoker university students [9 female, age range 18 to 38 years, mean 21.07, standard deviation (SD) 3.58] participated in the study, who regularly consume 1–2 cups of tea/coffee by self-report.

span.label: repeated measures ANOVA with Tukey HSD
span.term: repeated measures ANOVA with Tukey HSD
span.quote: The Tukey HSD post hoc test indicated that the High RT shortened in the caffeine (p < 0.039) and combined (p < 0.023) treatments compared to control

span.label: additive model of sum versus simultaneous
span.term: additive model of sum versus simultaneous
span.quote: To reveal potential interactions of caffeine and UMTS MP exposure in RT and oscillatory measures we focused on the exposure block and we used the additive analysis model with the following formula, as applied elsewhere 42 , 43 , 44 : Hereafter, “[Caffeine − Control] + [UMTS − Control]” and “Combined − Control” are referred to as ‘sum’ and ‘simultaneous’ data, respectively. We hypothesized that violation of the additivity of the analyzed RT or spectral amplitude measures would indicate synergistic interactions.

span.label: partial eta-squared
span.quote: There were significant differences between the analyzed trial numbers across the Probability categories (Low, High) [F(1,20) = 0.001; p = 0.98; partial eta-squared < 0.01] or Treatment (Control, UMTS, Caffeine, Combined) [F(3,60) = 0.34; p = 0.79; partial eta-squared < 0.02].

span.label: linear-log model
span.quote: The linear-log statistical model [y = a*log(x) + b] showed significantly decreasing (p < 0.001) logarithmic correlation (R 2 = 0.8832) between the target-target probabilities and the reaction times.

span.label: Reaction times were significantly faster to targets preceded by four standards (High local probability) than to targets preceded by one standard (Low local probability).
span.quote: In the present study RTs were highly dependent on the number of standard stimuli preceding the targets, namely RTs significantly decreased for targets with higher local probability (High, preceded by 4 standards) compared to low probability targets (Low, preceded by 1 standard).

span.label: Caffeine shortened reaction time only for High local probability targets, not for Low probability ones.
span.quote: Caffeine treatment significantly decreased the High probability RT relative to the Control (placebo).

span.label: Caffeine reduced pre-target alpha amplitude in both the Low and the High probability conditions relative to placebo.
span.quote: Caffeine significantly decreased both Low and High probability Alpha1 amplitudes relative to the Control.

span.label: Pre-target gamma amplitude was lower when the target was highly expected and faster responses accompanied that lower gamma.
span.quote: In line with their results, in the present study, in the pre-target period, we found lower gamma amplitude with faster RT in the High local probability condition and higher gamma amplitude with slower RT in the Low local probability condition.

span.label: UMTS mobile-phone-like exposure did not change reaction time.
span.quote: In line with the results of previous studies 50 , 51 we found no evidence that UMTS exposure alters RT.

span.label: UMTS exposure did not change pre-target alpha or gamma power either.
span.quote: The present results showing no effect of UMTS MP-like exposure on the alpha and gamma power in the pre-target period correspond well with previous studies using resting EEG, where also no effects of UMTS exposure were reported on brain oscillations 2 , 37 , 57 , 58 .

span.label: Caffeine and UMTS exposure did not interact: the combined condition produced no effect beyond the sum of the single exposures, on either behaviour or oscillations.
span.quote: Furthermore, we found no evidence of any interaction between caffeine and UMTS exposure on either RT or brain oscillations (spectral amplitude) using rANOVA or the additive analysis models.

span.label: The multiple regression models found no Probability-by-Treatment interaction, which undercuts the interpretation that caffeine acts by sharpening stimulus expectancy.
span.quote: However, the results of the multiple regression models showed no interaction effects between the target Probability and Treatments which support a different possible explanation of the present results.

span.label: The pre-registered hypothesis that simultaneous caffeine and mobile phone exposure would exceed either exposure alone was not supported.
span.quote: Our hypothesis was that, due to previously reported 1 , 6 similar facilitatory effects on brain excitatory activity, simultaneous caffeine and MP exposure will have a larger effect than caffeine or MP EMF exposure alone.

span.label: reaction time fell as local target probability rose, fitting a logarithmic model with R-squared 0.88
span.quote: The linear-log statistical model [y = a*log(x) + b] showed significantly decreasing (p < 0.001) logarithmic correlation (R 2 = 0.8832) between the target-target probabilities and the reaction times.

span.label: High probability trials were about 44 ms faster than Low
span.quote: The analysis of the Low (mean: 442.22 ms, SEM: 10.16) and High (mean: 398.54 ms, SEM: 9.71) probability categories revealed that they significantly differed from each other [F(1,22) = 102.584, p < 0.001, eta-squared = 0.823].

span.label: caffeine shortened reaction time only in High probability trials
span.quote: The Tukey HSD post hoc test indicated that the High RT shortened in the caffeine (p < 0.039) and combined (p < 0.023) treatments compared to control

span.label: caffeine reduced both alpha bands relative to placebo
span.quote: Tukey HSD post hoc analysis revealed significant amplitude decrease of both alpha bands [alpha1 (p < 0.005), alpha2 (p < 0.005)] in the caffeine treatment compared to control.

span.label: UMTS exposure alone or combined altered neither reaction time nor pre-stimulus oscillations
span.quote: However, in the present pharmacologically validated study UMTS exposure either alone or in combination with caffeine did not alter RT or pre-stimulus oscillatory brain activity.

span.label: the additive model showed no synergy on reaction time
span.quote: The summative analysis did not show any synergistic interactions on the RT.

span.label: the additive model showed no synergy on either alpha band
span.quote: The rANOVA [(sum vs. simultaneous) X Probability X Electrode] of the summative model indicated no synergistic interactions of caffeine and UMTS exposure on either alpha1 or alpha2 frequency bands.

span.label: the overall treatment effect on reaction time did not survive post hoc testing
span.quote: However the Treatment effect did not survive the post hoc analyses.

span.label: Low vs. High local target probability categories
span.term: Low vs. High local target probability categories
span.quote: In the Low probability category and in the High probability category 1 and 4 standard stimuli preceded the target, respectively.

span.label: synergistic interaction, operationalised as a violation of additivity
span.term: synergistic interaction, operationalised as a violation of additivity
span.quote: We hypothesized that violation of the additivity of the analyzed RT or spectral amplitude measures would indicate synergistic interactions.

span.label: local probability categories (Prob1-Prob7)
span.quote: The procedure resulted in 7 different stimulus categories according to target local probability (Prob) from category 1 to category 7.

span.label: Low and High local probability
span.quote: Data from Prob1 trials where only one standard stimulus preceded the target were assigned to the low probability (Low) category while data from Prob4 trials where four standard stimuli preceded the target were assigned to the high probability category (High) and were selected for further analysis.

span.label: the additive synergy model
span.quote: To reveal potential interactions of caffeine and UMTS MP exposure in RT and oscillatory measures we focused on the exposure block and we used the additive analysis model with the following formula, as applied elsewhere 42 , 43 , 44 : Hereafter, “[Caffeine − Control] + [UMTS − Control]” and “Combined − Control” are referred to as ‘sum’ and ‘simultaneous’ data, respectively. We hypothesized that violation of the additivity of the analyzed RT or spectral amplitude measures would indicate synergistic interactions.

span.label: caffeine treatment (3 mg/kg vs. glucose placebo capsule)
span.term: caffeine treatment (3 mg/kg vs. glucose placebo capsule)
span.quote: Three mg/kg caffeine packed in identical hard gelatin capsules were administered to the participants.

span.label: UMTS mobile-phone RF exposure (genuine vs. sham)
span.term: UMTS mobile-phone RF exposure (genuine vs. sham)
span.quote: Double-blind experimental conditions were ensured by a two-position switch (A or B) located on the front panel of the RF amplifier: one position was associated with genuine exposure, and the other with sham exposure.

span.label: local target probability (Low = 1 preceding standard vs. High = 4 preceding standards)
span.term: local target probability (Low = 1 preceding standard vs. High = 4 preceding standards)
span.quote: Data from Prob1 trials where only one standard stimulus preceded the target were assigned to the low probability (Low) category while data from Prob4 trials where four standard stimuli preceded the target were assigned to the high probability category (High) and were selected for further analysis.

span.label: reaction time to target stimuli
span.quote: In a full factorial experimental design, 25 participants performed a simple visual target detection task while reaction time (RT) and electroencephalogram (EEG) was recorded.

span.label: pre-target alpha-band power (amplitude)
span.quote: We analyzed single trial RT and alpha-band power (amplitude) in the pre-target interval.

span.label: smoking status (non-smokers only)
span.quote: Because the half-life of caffeine in the body is reduced by 30 to 50% in smokers compared to nonsmokers 13 , here we enrolled only nonsmokers.

span.label: number of capsules taken (held identical across placebo and caffeine sessions)
span.term: number of capsules taken (held identical across placebo and caffeine sessions)
span.quote: To avoid possible influences caused by subjective bias on the number of capsules taken, volunteers received the same amount of capsules in the control (placebo) sessions as in the caffeine sessions.

span.label: prior caffeine and alcohol abstinence before each session
span.term: prior caffeine and alcohol abstinence before each session
span.quote: Participants were asked to abstain from any kind of caffeine-containing substances and alcohol at least 10 and 24 hour prior to each session, respectively.

span.label: pre-target spectral amplitude entered as a predictor alongside treatment in the RT regression
span.term: pre-target spectral amplitude entered as a predictor alongside treatment in the RT regression
span.quote: First, to address the question whether any treatment (UMTS, Caffeine, or Combined) affects the RT, we applied categorical variables on Treatments where Control treatment served as reference also controlling for probabilities and pre-target spectral amplitude as predictor variables.

span.label: target probability as a modulator of the caffeine effect
span.term: target probability as a modulator of the caffeine effect
span.quote: The interaction test between the Probability and the Treatments allows us to investigate whether or not the caffeine effect was modulated by the target probability.

span.label: target-to-target distance
span.quote: Data from Prob1 trials where only one standard stimulus preceded the target were assigned to the low probability (Low) category while data from Prob4 trials where four standard stimuli preceded the target were assigned to the high probability category (High) and were selected for further analysis.

span.quote: In a full factorial experimental design, 25 participants performed a simple visual target detection task while reaction time (RT) and electroencephalogram (EEG) was recorded.

span.quote: The trial numbers for standard and deviant stimuli were 640 and 160, respectively.
